review_notes: I read the whole file, lines 1–151. It has no new definitions, structures or classes. It contains only theorems, such as the existence of a reversal-compatible algebra equivalence and the simple, central and degree results for the even Clifford algebra. These theorems use existing concepts (`even`, `CliffordAlgebra`, `IsSimpleRing`, `Algebra.IsCentral`, `Algebra.deg`) and helper declarations from other files. The rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication, so nothing here competes with an existing Mathlib concept. The comment in `isCentral_even_of_odd_finrank` explains why the universe-heterogeneous `Algebra.IsCentral.of_algEquiv` argument is repeated, and I treated that as proof-level, not as a competing concept. I did not open the Mathlib sources, so I cannot rule out a deeper duplicate in the imported TauCeti files. The only other uncertainty is the same: whether a theorem restates a Mathlib one.
